summary: The folded breastpiece measures a span on each side. Isaiah asks whose hand could measure the heavens in the same way.

senses.definition: A length measured from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger when the hand is spread.

evidence.note: The instructions give the square breastpiece a length and width of one span each.
The finished breastpiece has those dimensions when doubled.
A span is added to a count of cubits in the description of Goliath’s height.
Measuring the heavens with a span stands beside measuring the waters in the hollow of a hand.
The altar’s rim measures one span. The same verse uses a handbreadth to specify the cubit.

cognates.gloss: distance from thumb to little finger

evidence.locator: s.v. ܙܪܬܐ, measure of twelve fingers

note: Jewish Aramaic, Syriac and Mandaic all attest the measure. Inheritance and borrowing are difficult to distinguish here. Egyptian ḏr.t means ‘hand’ and can denote a handful by volume (TLA 184630). The proposed Egyptian origin would require a shift to a measure of length. The Hebrew passages give no fixed modern equivalent.
